comments.content: The shared filter condition `notWorkflow(t) && !t.archived && !t.deletedAt` is duplicated across `visible` and `doneList`. Extract into a single predicate (e.g., `const listable = (t) => notWorkflow(t) && !t.archived && !t.deletedAt`) so future changes (e.g., adding another hidden state) only need one edit.

reloadTasks and the inline onTasksReload arrow are recreated on every render. Combined with setTaskColumn / updateTask (also plain function declarations in the component body), every App state change produces brand-new prop references for WorkflowPage, defeating React.memo in TaskNode and GoalNode and forcing the whole canvas to re-render. Wrap reloadTasks in useCallback and either pass it directly to onTasksReload (letting WorkflowPage handle its own error via the handleCommandError it already imports) or memoize the inline arrow. For consistency, setTaskColumn and updateTask should also be useCallback'd — they are passed to both KanbanBoard and WorkflowPage.

The inline arrow for onTasksReload is recreated on every render. Combined with the unmemoized reloadTasks (and the already-unmemoized setTaskColumn / updateTask passed alongside), this defeats the React.memo wrappers on TaskNode / GoalNode. Either pass reloadTasks directly (WorkflowPage can .catch its own errors via the handleCommandError it already imports) or wrap this inline arrow in useCallback.

The invisible `Handle type="target"` contradicts the docstring's "不参与连线" claim. React Flow still treats this as a valid connection endpoint (the parent's `isValidConnection` is what blocks it). The Handle serves no functional or visual purpose here and creates a misleading design signal — consider removing it entirely.

comments.content: The `dependsOn` branch only rejects empty-string elements. It does not reject self-reference (`task.id` listed in its own `depends_on`), cycles among DAG nodes, or IDs that don't exist among the workflow's other nodes. `build_dag` in `workflow_runner.rs` does reject cycles and dangling refs at execution time (see `build_dag_rejects_cycle_and_dangling` at workflow_runner.rs:573), but that means the patch is accepted eagerly and the error is deferred until the user actually runs the workflow — losing the "fail fast at write time" contract that other validation branches (e.g. empty title, unknown key) provide. Consider either validating self-reference / existence against `load_tasks_by_workflow` siblings here, or at minimum surfacing a clear error hint that cycle/dangling checks happen at `workflow_run` time.

The new validation branches (`origin`, `workflowId`, `dependsOn`, `canvasPos`) and the new `load_tasks_by_workflow` reader have no dedicated tests. The diff refactors the existing `task_set_column_tests` / `task_patch_tests` / `task_reorder_tests` `setup_conn` helpers to use the shared `TASKS_DDL`, but adds zero new test cases for the four new branches in `apply_task_patch`, the `depends_on` JSON-corruption fallback in `task_from_row` (line 481-491), or the "origin: 'user' normalizes to None" / "workflowId empty-after-trim rejected" / "canvas_pos half-written row reads as None" contracts. Without tests these branches can silently regress. Add at minimum: (1) `apply_task_patch` happy + reject path for each of the four new keys, (2) `task_from_row` round-trip preserving the new fields, (3) `load_tasks_by_workflow` returning only non-soft-deleted rows for the given workflow_id, (4) `depends_on` corruption recovery.

`Task::origin` is exposed as `Option<String>` despite this diff also introducing `TASK_ORIGIN_USER` / `TASK_ORIGIN_WORKFLOW` constants and only ever storing two distinct values. The runtime string-comparison / "user" → `None` normalization logic in the `"origin"` branch below only exists because the type system can't represent the two-state domain. A typed enum (e.g. `pub enum TaskOrigin { User, Workflow }` with custom Serde producing `"user"`/`"workflow"`) would make invalid states unrepresentable at compile time and eliminate the normalization branch. The current design is acceptable, but worth flagging per the "model domain states with enums, not strings" rule.

`canvas_x` and `canvas_y` are read and written as `Option<f64>` with no `is_finite()` guard. The write path (`set_from` → `serde_json`) and the read path (`row.get(25)` / `row.get(26)`) propagate NaN and ±Infinity into the struct unchanged. SQLite stores these faithfully as IEEE 754 doubles, and `serde_json` cannot serialize NaN/±Infinity by default — so a poisoned coordinate (e.g. crafted `{"x": 1e500}` overflowing to Infinity, or arithmetic producing NaN) would crash every downstream Tauri payload serialization that flows through `load_tasks_by_workflow` / `load_all` / `tasks_export` / `tasks-updated` broadcasts. Add an `is_finite()` check on the upsert side (preferred: clamp or reject via `CommandError::InvalidArgument`) and at minimum guard the read side so a stale DB row doesn't take down the whole task list.

`workflow_id` lacks referential integrity. `TASKS_DDL` declares it as a plain `TEXT` column with no `REFERENCES workflows(id)` clause, the `W1_TASK_COLUMNS` migration in `open_db` (db/mod.rs:195-207) only adds it as `TEXT`, and the `"workflowId"` branch below only rejects empty-after-trim strings — any non-existent workflow id is accepted at write time. The current orphan risk is bounded because `workflow_delete` (db/workflow.rs:956) cascades hard-deletes node tasks inside a transaction, but until that delete path runs, a `task_patch` could silently bind a task to a workflow id that was never created (e.g. via the public REST surface or a future caller). Consider adding `FOREIGN KEY (workflow_id) REFERENCES workflows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` either in `TASKS_DDL` or via an idempotent migration in `open_db`, or at minimum validating `workflow_id` existence here via a `load_workflow` lookup.

Silent failure when persistence fails: `setDecomposeGuidance` returns `false` when `localStorage` is unavailable (privacy mode, quota exceeded, etc., per `workflowPrompt.ts` OCR r1). When `ok === false`, `setGuidanceSaved(false)` only hides the indicator — the user has no signal that their edits weren't actually saved. Consider surfacing an explicit error (e.g., a transient "保存失败" toast, or holding `guidanceSaved === false` plus a small inline error label) so a failed save isn't indistinguishable from the normal "no changes since last save" state. The OCR r1 contract in `workflowPrompt.ts` only forbids falsely showing "已保存"; it doesn't forbid showing a dedicated failure message.

Atomicity violation: `upsert_workflow` runs against `conn` outside the explicit `conn.transaction()` opened below. If `upsert_tasks`, `delete_tasks`, or `tx.commit()` fails, the workflow row is already durably written while its node tasks may be missing or stale — contradicting the "锁内事务" guarantee in the section header. Sibling paths in this file (`workflow_delete`) and in `db/tasks.rs` (`task_patch_locked`, `task_set_column_locked`) all open `tx` first and run every write inside it. Move the workflow-row upsert (and the dependent `existing_fps` / `free_by_fp` / `real_id` precomputation that needs the persisted id) to *after* `tx` is opened, or restructure so the workflow row is written through `&tx` rather than `conn`.

Production panic risk: `.expect("kept 节点必在 existing 中")` will kill the worker thread on a logic regression and surface as a `spawn_blocking` join error to the user. The invariant is strong today (we just assigned `real_id[i] = existing[j].id.clone()` for a `j` that was an index into `existing`), but this is the kind of "should never happen" that's better expressed as a `debug_assert!` or a typed `CommandError` so a regression shows up as a recoverable failure rather than a process panic.

comments.content: Inconsistent time source inside the same file: `workflow_save` reads `let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis();` once and passes it into `workflow_save_locked(&mut conn, input, now)`, making the time axis testable. `workflow_rename` instead calls `chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis()` inside the spawn_blocking closure, so "no-op when name unchanged" and "updated_at is exactly N" can't be asserted without sleeping. Mirror `workflow_save_locked`'s pattern: hoist the clock read into the `#[tauri::command]` wrapper and pass `now` into a `_locked` helper.

NaN ordering collapses to `Equal` and silently corrupts the topological export order. `partial_cmp` returns `None` whenever either `order` is NaN; the `unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)` swallows that signal, so a `tasks.order` row with NaN (possible via JSON `null`/missing round-trips) is sorted as if equal to whatever came before it — and `dependsOn` can then reference nodes that don't appear upstream in `file.nodes`. Either reject NaN explicitly or use a total-order helper that surfaces the bad row.

`depends_on.contains(&d)` inside the dedup loop is O(n²); the bound is small (≤30) but the loop also unconditionally allocates a fresh `Vec<String>` per node. Use a `HashSet` for the seen-set to make intent clearer and scale linearly.

Unused tuple destructure: both slots (`p.name`, `name.clone()`) are discarded — the actual `name` used by the `upsert_workflow` call below comes from the outer `name` binding. The intermediate tuple and the `name.clone()` allocation are dead and obscure intent.

comments.content: `workflow_rename` is the only write command in this file that does not broadcast on the existing `tasks-changed` / `tasks-updated` channels. After a rename, any UI window that already cached the workflow's old name keeps showing it. Either add the broadcast (rename touches nothing in `tasks`, so a dedicated `workflows-changed` event would be more honest) or document the listener contract — silence here is a divergence from every other write path in the file.

Draft input causes a re-render storm on every keystroke. In WorkflowPage.tsx:609-612, `onDraftTitleCommit` is an inline arrow inside the `rfNodes` `useMemo` factory that calls `setNodes((prev) => prev.map(...))` — replacing the entire `nodes` array on every character. Because `nodes` is in the `rfNodes` memo deps (line 629), the entire `rfNodes` array (all task nodes, their `data` objects, the goal node) is rebuilt every keystroke, forcing React Flow to re-render every node and re-derive every edge. In practice this also breaks the input itself: React Flow's keyed reconciliation remounts the node when its position/identity churns during a typing burst, which loses caret position / focus mid-word. Two pragmatic fixes: (a) hold draft titles in a separate `Map<localId, string>` state so typing only mutates one key without rebuilding `nodes`, and only sync into the CanvasNode on commit/blur; or (b) route the keystroke handler through a `nodesRef` (the same `tasksRef`/`propsRef` pattern already used at WorkflowPage.tsx:96-101) so typing doesn't trigger a `setNodes`. Either way, `data.onDraftTitleCommit` should not be defined inside the `rfNodes` memo.
comments.existing_code: onChange={(e) => data.onDraftTitleCommit(id, e.target.value)}

comments.content: `memo` on TaskNode is effectively decorative given how the parent assembles `data`. In WorkflowPage.tsx:606-617 the entire `TaskNodeData` object (including all callbacks) is reconstructed inside the `rfNodes` `useMemo` factory on every memo recomputation. Even though `commitTitle` / `toggleDone` / `toggleSubtask` / `deleteNode` are themselves `useCallback`-stable, the wrapping `data` object is fresh, so React's referential equality check in `memo` always fails and TaskNode re-renders unconditionally. To make memo useful, either pass primitives + a single stable dispatcher object (e.g. `{ task, draftTitle, actions }` where `actions` is a `useMemo`-stable object holding the four callbacks), or move callbacks off `data` into a context/ref that TaskNode subscribes to. Without this change, the `memo` wrapper gives a false sense of optimization.

`nodeBorder` conflates two distinct cases under "green ring". The comment says "done 无 result = 用户手动完成 → 绿", but the implementation keys on `task.result?.status === undefined`, which also matches a task that *has* a `result` object whose `status` field happens to be undefined (e.g. legacy rows missing `status`, partial save, or deserialization hiccup — see types.ts:111-117 where `status?` is genuinely optional). Such tasks would silently render green even if the bot run didn't actually succeed. Tighten the check to `task.result === undefined || task.result.status === undefined || task.result.status === "success"`, and ideally document the legacy/partial-data case so it isn't mistaken for a manual-complete.

**Critical: controller deadlocks when any node is `done+success` (every breakpoint-resume run).**

`build_dag` excludes done+success nodes from `ready` and from `dependents` keys (correct for execution semantics — they must not be re-executed), but still includes them in `dag.nodes` (line 110). The controller sets `total = dag.nodes.len()` (line 307) and only populates `resolved` from `NodeOutcome` (line 367); done nodes are never spawned and never inserted into `resolved`. So `while resolved.len() < total` (line 360) never becomes true and the controller blocks forever in `rx.recv().await` — only breakable by an external `workflow_stop`. This is reachable on every breakpoint-resume run with ≥1 already-done node, and also when `to_run == 0` (all nodes already done). Fix options: (a) pre-seed `resolved` with the done-node IDs before entering the loop (and add `already_done` to `done_count` for the final audit); (b) compute `total` as `tasks.iter().filter(|t| !is_success(t)).count()` instead of `dag.nodes.len()`; (c) short-circuit `workflow_run` and skip spawning the controller when `to_run == 0`.
comments.existing_code: let total = dag.nodes.len();

comments.content:
**Audit and notification understate `done` and inflate `skipped` on breakpoint-resume runs.**

`already_done` is computed in `workflow_run` (line 215) but is never folded back into `done_count` or `total` before the final `audit::write_event("workflow_run_done", ...)` (line 447) and `notify_workflow_done(...)` (line 452). For a 10-node workflow where 5 were already done and 3 new ones complete in this run, the user sees `done=3, skipped=2, total=10` and the notification body reads "3/10 节点完成" — when 8 are actually completed. Add `already_done` to both `done_count` before constructing `done`, and to `total` (or define `total` here as the active-node count to match what was actually executed), and propagate the same corrected values into `notify_workflow_done`.

**O(N²) DB load per node completion — single-row API already exists.**

Both the success re-check after `run_task_in_chat` (lines 336-340) and `mark_skipped` (line 457) call `crate::db::db_load(...)` which always loads the full task table (`db_load_for` → `load_all`, see `src-tauri/src/db/tasks.rs:601`), then `.into_iter().find(|t| t.id == ...)` to inspect a single row. Per workflow this is N full-table scans, giving O(N²) DB work for `spawn_node` plus another O(N²) for `mark_skipped`. The single-task PK lookup `db::tasks::load_task(conn, &id)` (`db/tasks.rs:547`) — already in production use by `bot_orchestrator` and `exec_steps` — is the right primitive. Wrap it in a `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking` like `load_workflow_tasks` does, or add a thin `db_load_one` async wrapper, and use it in both spots.

**`mark_skipped` does the same O(N²) full-table load — use the single-row lookup here too.**

`mark_skipped` (line 457) calls `db_load` then `.find()` — same anti-pattern as `spawn_node`. With M skipped/affected nodes per workflow run, this is M full table scans. Switch to `db::tasks::load_task` via a blocking task; on `None` (task deleted in the meantime) no-op silently. Also consider whether `db_upsert` will reliably accept a single-element `Vec<Task>` here — `db_upsert` (`db/tasks.rs:608`) takes `Vec<Task>`, which matches the current call.

**Controller hangs indefinitely if any spawned node task panics before `tx.send`.**

`rx.recv().await` (line 364) has no timeout, no panic recovery, and no `JoinHandle` retained for the spawned `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` tasks (line 320). If a panic occurs inside `SubagentGate::wait_slot_cancellable` or inside `run_task_in_chat` before the `NodeOutcome` is queued, that worker task dies silently, no outcome is ever delivered, and the controller blocks on `rx.recv()` forever — the cancel flag is only set by an external user-driven `workflow_stop`, so the workflow appears permanently "running" in the registry. Add at least: (a) wrap the spawned async body in `std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe` + `tokio::spawn` catch_unwind, sending a synthetic `NodeOutcome { ok: false, cancelled: false }` on panic; or (b) attach a watchdog timeout to `rx.recv()`; or (c) retain `JoinHandle`s in a `Vec` and `select!` on them with cancellation.

**`mark_skipped` silently swallows all errors — no audit/log on failure.**

`db_load` failure and `db_upsert` failure are both discarded (`if let Ok(cur)` and `.is_ok()`), so a transient DB error during cancellation cleanup leaves the task visually un-skipped with zero diagnostic. Combined with the O(N²) load, this is the highest-frequency error site in the file. At minimum, log via `crate::audit::write_event(... AuditLevel::Warn, "workflow_skip_failed", ...)` on each `Err`, matching the rest of the file's logging discipline (e.g., `workflow_run_done` lines 436-451).

**Notification send failure logged via `eprintln!` instead of the structured audit channel.**

The rest of the file uses `crate::audit::write_event` for every operational signal (start/stop/run_done). A failed OS notification (often a permission denial — "未授权") is exactly the kind of thing users will want to be able to grep the audit log for; `eprintln!` (line 478) bypasses that channel entirely. Route this through `audit::write_event(..., AuditLevel::Warn, "workflow_notify_failed", &[("err", e.to_string())])` for consistency.

Macro hygiene: `$err` is interpolated twice (in `$err.to_string()` and `return Err($err)`). Per the macro-hygiene rule, an expression fragment should be bound once so caller-supplied expressions with side effects don't run twice — current call sites (`fail!(e)`) happen to pass a plain local, but a future `fail!(some_fn())` would silently invoke the function twice. Fix by capturing once: `let err = $err; last_err = err.to_string(); ... return Err(err);`.

Asymmetric validation: `title` is trimmed and rejected when empty, but `note` is only checked for the upper char cap. `Some("")` and `Some("   ")` pass validation and get persisted, which renders as blank/whitespace notes on the WorkflowCanvas. Either trim+drop empty notes here, or document the asymmetry and rely on the downstream `TaskCardContent` to skip rendering. If trimming, also reduce to `Option<String>` semantics (None vs Some(trimmed)).

Duplicate indices inside a single `depends_on` (e.g. `[0, 0]`) are not rejected. Downstream `graph.ts:64` calls `g.setEdge(d, n.localId)` once per entry, and the rest of the pipeline will treat the card as having a 2-edge upstream dependency. W4-TEMPLATE spec explicitly does "dependsOn 重复元素自动去重" — the same dedup should happen here at the validation boundary. Also reject references equal to `i` (self-loop) explicitly with a distinct error message; the current message lumps self-loop and reverse-reference together but the value diagnostics differ.

User-facing `reason` strings embed Rust identifiers and the raw field name `dependsOn` (`第 {} 个任务的 dependsOn 含非法下标 {d}（必须引用更靠前的任务，下标 < {i}）`). The `{d}` and `{i}` interpolation leaks the inner enum-index variable names to end users, mixes Chinese/English, and is brittle if the field is ever renamed. Consider routing these through a stable i18n message id or at least dropping the `{d}` and `{i}` from the public-facing string.

comments.content:
The node container has no `relative` positioning class, but the delete button uses `absolute -right-2 -top-2`. Verified `.nm-card` in `src/ui/main.css` (L157-164) only sets border-radius / bg / border / shadow / transition — **no `position: relative`**. Result: the absolutely-positioned button will resolve against the nearest *positioned* ancestor (likely the React Flow viewport / pane). When the node is dragged or the canvas pans, the button will visually detach from the card. Add `relative` to the wrapper (or `relative` to the button itself's positioning context) so the button tracks the card.

```tsx
<div className={`relative nm-card w-[340px] px-1 pt-1 pb-2 ${nodeBorder(task)}`}>
```

Severity is medium because the button is currently misplaced from day one (not just on style refactors) — it just happens to land somewhere unnoticeable until the user pans/zooms.

comments.content: Critical TOCTOU race in `workflow_run`: the `contains_key` check at lines 208-215 and the `insert` at line 227 are guarded by **separate** lock acquisitions. Between them the registry mutex is released across the `await load_workflow_tasks(...)`, so two concurrent `workflow_run` calls for the same `workflow_id` can both pass the "not in map" check, both load tasks, and both insert. Result: two controllers race on the same workflow, spawning each ready node twice and emitting duplicate `workflow_run_done` audits / system notifications. Fix: keep one lock acquisition across both the membership check and the insert (move the load inside the lock or restructure as a single critical section using `entry().or_insert_with(|| ...)`).

`build_dag` is O(N×D) due to a nested linear scan: for each dep `d`, it calls `tasks.iter().find(|x| x.id == **d)` to check upstream success status. With N nodes and D total dependencies this is O(N·D); for a workflow with 200 nodes averaging 2 deps each that's 40k comparisons. Pre-compute an id→&Task `HashMap` (or just an id→bool done map) once at the top of the function and use it for both the `ids` set and the upstream lookup, reducing to O(N+D).

Error context is dropped when a node task fails. When `run_task_in_chat` returns `Err(_)`, the code collapses it to `ok = false` (line 345) and proceeds to propagate the `skip_closure`. The actual error message is never audited or logged — users see a cascade of `⏭ 因上游「X」失败未执行` notes but have no record of the original failure (rate-limit? LLM crash? key missing?). Emit at least an audit event with the workflow id, node id, and error message so `workflow_run_done` users can debug. The `Ok(_)` branch already re-reads the row, so the symmetric path is to log on `Err`.

`running.lock()` is acquired per downstream node inside the success branch (line 389) and once per candidate during the cancellation cleanup loop (line 425). Each `lock()` is an uncontended Mutex acquisition (cheap) but it serializes against `spawn_node` (which also locks on insert/remove) and adds measurable overhead when a single upstream has many descendants. Hoist the lock once per outcome in the success branch (collect the free set into a local `HashSet`) and once per cleanup pass to amortize the cost.

`by_id` is built with `iter().enumerate().map(...).collect()` which loses information when two tasks share the same `id` — the first index is silently overwritten by the last. The DB schema declares `id` as PRIMARY KEY so it shouldn't happen in practice, but a corrupted DB or a future bug that inserts duplicate rows would cause `task_fp_at` to walk the wrong branch and produce a fingerprint that does not reflect the actual graph. Consider `.collect::<Result<_, _>>()` against a duplicate-detection step (e.g. scan + assert, or build `Vec<(&str, usize)>` and detect collisions explicitly).

When a node is kept, `j` was already known at the moment `real_id[i] = existing[j].id.clone()` (line 421), but it was discarded and the kept branch does an O(n) `existing.iter().find(|t| t.id == real_id[i])` lookup again. With N≤30 this is cheap, but the re-lookup obscures the fact that `kept_flags[i]` is paired with a known `existing` index. Stash the `kept_j` index alongside `kept_flags` and use `existing[kept_j[i]].clone()` directly — cheaper and avoids the `.expect` invariant on `real_id[i]`.

With N≤30 this is cheap, but the re-lookup obscures the fact that `kept_flags[i]` is paired with a known `existing` index. Stash the `kept_j` index alongside `kept_flags` and use `existing[kept_j[i] as usize].clone()` directly — cheaper and removes the `.expect` invariant on `real_id[i]`.

The DB schema declares `id` as PRIMARY KEY so it shouldn't happen in practice, but a corrupted DB or a future bug that inserts duplicate rows would cause `task_fp_at` to walk the wrong branch and produce a fingerprint that does not reflect the actual graph. Detect duplicates while building `by_id` and log a warning so the corruption is observable instead of silent.

Workflow.createdAt/updatedAt are epoch ms (mirrors Task.updatedAt at line 92 which documents it as such), but the field comments are missing here. Add `/** epoch ms */` to both for consistency with the existing Task.updatedAt convention and to make the unit explicit since the Rust WORKFLOWS_DDL stores them as plain INTEGER without a unit comment either.

`audit::write_event` is a synchronous function that performs filesystem I/O (resolves `data_dir`, rotates the log, appends a line). Calling it from the async `workflow_decompose` function blocks the Tauri async-runtime thread for the duration of the file write. Per the async-safety checklist this should be spawned off (`tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`) or wrapped in a non-blocking audit sink so a slow disk doesn't stall the command.

The call sites are the two `crate::audit::write_event(...)` invocations inside `workflow_decompose` (success path and the `fail!` macro).

The retry loop has no backoff or timeout. On validation failure the next LLM call is issued immediately (up to 2 attempts total). A transient issue (rate limit, slow provider, deterministic model failure) is amplified rather than dampened, and there is no cancellation propagation: if the Tauri window is closed mid-retry, `summarize_messages` cannot observe cancellation. Per the async-safety checklist, bounded retries should also include at least a small delay (or `tokio::time::sleep`) and should respect the `tauri::async_runtime` cancellation token. Also worth adding a `tokio::time::timeout` around `summarize_messages` so a hung provider can't pin the command indefinitely.

Contract and validation disagree on the upper bound. The contract tells the model `subtasks：1 到 20 个元素` but `validate_decompose` enforces `MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES = 30` (imported from `db::workflow`). A model that obeys the contract literally will cap at 20 even when 21–30 would be valid; conversely, the model is told 21–30 are out-of-spec. Either relax the contract to match `MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES` ("1 到 {MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES} 个元素") or tighten the validator — but the two must agree.

comments.content: The success audit event omits an `outcome` field while the failure path emits `("outcome", "failed")`. This makes log filtering ("show all workflow_decompose outcomes") inconsistent. For symmetry, add `("outcome", "success".to_string())` (or use a stable `status` field on both paths) so downstream auditing and alerting can rely on a single key.

`draftFromDecompose` blindly indexes `nodes[d]` from LLM-returned indices with no defensive check. The comment claims the server guarantees `d < i`, but if validation is ever bypassed (e.g., a future schema change, an alternate entry point, or LLM-side schema drift), `nodes[d]` can be `undefined` and crash on `.localId`. Negative or non-integer indices would also throw. At minimum, filter to in-range indices and dedupe — Rust's `validate_decompose` enforces forward-only but does not dedupe (see `workflow.rs` test `{"dependsOn": ["n1", "n1"]}`), so duplicate edges can leak into dagre here too.

`draftFromTasks` keeps `dependsOn` entries whose ids aren't in the reconstructed `nodes` array. `rfEdges` and `layoutGraph` both filter dangling refs at render/layout time, but the dangling ids are persisted on the save payload and round-trip back through `workflow_load`, so the dirt accumulates across save/load cycles. Recommend filtering `dependsOn` to ids present in the input `tasks` set so the model is consistent at every layer.

comments.content: `if (from === to) return true;` is redundant: BFS initializes the stack with `to` and the first iteration checks `cur === from`, which equals `to`, so the self-loop case is already covered. Harmless, but the duplication obscures the BFS invariant.

The comment says "缺坐标的行补 dagre 布局" (rows missing coords get dagre layout), but the implementation re-lays out the *entire* graph whenever *any* row is missing `canvasPos`, discarding the user's hand-placed positions for the other nodes. Either change the comment to match the actual "all-or-nothing" semantics, or do a partial layout that only assigns positions to the missing nodes and keeps saved positions for the rest.

Validation gap: the dependsOn branch only rejects empty-string elements. Duplicate IDs within the same list (`["a", "a", "b"]`) pass through and are only silently deduplicated later by `build_dag` via its local `HashSet` (workflow_runner.rs:53-63). Pushing duplicate rejection to execution time means the JSON stored in the DB carries redundant edges that have to be reconciled at every DAG build. Reject duplicates here so the stored representation is canonical.

`workflow_id` is a plain `TEXT` column without an index, yet `load_tasks_by_workflow` filters by it and `workflow_run` calls it on every execution start. With many tasks in the DB (especially after workflows accumulate history), this becomes a full table scan. Consider adding `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_workflow_id ON tasks(workflow_id) WHERE workflow_id IS NOT NULL` alongside the W1-CANVAS migration in `open_db`. A partial index keeps the write cost minimal for the common case where most tasks have `workflow_id IS NULL` (user kanban cards).

The `TASK_ORIGIN_USER` constant exists for validation but is silently normalized to `None` on storage — so the value `"user"` is accepted as input, passes the whitelist check, then immediately becomes `None`. This makes the constant misleading (its only legal value is "user" → never persisted). Combined with `TASK_ORIGIN_WORKFLOW` being the only storage value, an enum would make the data model self-documenting: `pub origin: Option<TaskOrigin>` with variants `User` (== None) and `Workflow` (== Some(...)). The current `Option<String>` + post-hoc normalization is the same problem flagged for the type itself, but the silent drop of `"user"` is a distinct behavioral quirk worth fixing alongside.

`draftFromTasks` uses an inline `import("../../types").Task` type qualifier, which is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (e.g., `TaskNode.tsx`, `WidgetApp.tsx`, `ChatPanel.tsx`, `ArchivePage.tsx`, `KanbanBoard.tsx`, …) that all use a top-level `import type { Task } from "../../types"`. Move it to the file-level imports so the dependency on the shared type contract is grep-able and refactor-friendly.

comments.content: `wouldCreateCycle` rebuilds the entire downstream adjacency map from scratch on every invocation. In `WorkflowPage.tsx` it is wired into `isValidConnection`, which React Flow calls on every hover/drag tick while the user is dragging a connection. For an N-node workflow that is O(N·E) per call instead of O(reachable) for the search itself. Either accept a precomputed downstream map (or the nodes array + memoize the build), or use the cheaper "can `to` reach `from`" walk by reusing the map across calls during a single drag.

The single `armedTimerRef` is shared between two independent two-step confirmations. `deleteWorkflow` (line 558) and `regenerate` (line 268) both assign to the same ref. Scenario: user arms delete (T1 set), then arms regenerate (T2 set, T1 cleared). After 3s, T2 fires and sets `regenArmed=false` — meanwhile `deleteArmed` stays `true` because its T1 was cleared and never re-armed. The delete button keeps its red "armed" visual state with no pending timer to reset it, and any subsequent click is misinterpreted as the second confirm click. Use two separate refs (e.g. `deleteArmedTimerRef`, `regenArmedTimerRef`) and a `useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(...), [])` per ref, or merge into one `{kind, expiresAt}` state.

comments.content: TaskNode and GoalNode are both wrapped in `React.memo` (see their `import { memo }`), but the `data` objects constructed here contain freshly-instantiated arrow functions every render: `onDraftTitleCommit` (line 477), `onRename`/`onGoalChange` (lines 467-468). Combined with the `rfNodes` useMemo deps, the `data` prop identity changes on most parent re-renders, which makes `memo` a no-op. For boards with many nodes this re-renders every node on every state change. Hoist the callbacks via `useCallback` (e.g. `commitDraftTitle` analogous to `commitTitle`) and `useCallback` for the inline ones in GoalNode data.

`cancelDecompose` only bumps `decomposeSeqRef` so the late response is discarded (the comment explicitly says "v1 语义：忽略结果，非中断请求"). However, `workflow_decompose.rs` runs an LLM call (with one auto-retry on validation failure) that completes server-side regardless, consuming tokens. Users reasonably expect "取消" to abort the work. Either (a) expose a `workflow_decompose_cancel` Tauri command and have the backend set a stop flag checked between attempts, or (b) surface the limitation in the cancel button title ("取消仅丢弃前端结果，后端仍在跑"). The current behaviour silently wastes API budget on a click the user explicitly intended to abort.

The `useEffect(() => { tasksRef.current = tasks; ... })` has no dependency array, which is the discouraged "sync ref on every render" pattern. Per React's official guidance for "latest ref" (the useEffectEvent RFC), the modern recommendation is to assign during render (`tasksRef.current = tasks;` at top of the component body) — the eslint rule that warns about this is the legacy one. The trade-off comment ("render 期写 ref 会被 lint 拦") accepts a 1-tick stale window for callbacks fired from React Flow's internal node-data re-evaluation, which can produce stale reads in concurrent mode. Either assign during render, or capture the props via `useEffect` with explicit deps `[tasks, onSetColumn, onUpdate]` so updates are batched correctly.

Several fire-and-forget `invoke(...)` chains have no abort/cleanup: the initial `workflow_list` fetch (line ~125), the post-save `workflow_list` refresh (line ~524), and the 300 ms `setTimeout` inside `stopRun` (line ~432). Only the polling interval and the unmount cleanup useEffect handle cancellation. App.tsx switches views via `view === "workflow" ? <WorkflowPage /> : ...`, so WorkflowPage unmounts on tab switch — a late response will call `setState` on an unmounted instance (React 18 swallows the warning but it is wasted work, and the post-stop `setTimeout` can even invoke against a stale `wf`). Track an `AbortController` (Tauri commands accept an `AbortSignal`-like via the JS side) or guard via the existing `openSeqRef`/`decomposeSeqRef` pattern, and clear the `setTimeout` in the unmount cleanup.

In `onEdgesChange`, `const [, target] = c.id.split("->")` assumes every incoming `EdgeChange` id contains the literal `->`. If a React Flow internal change yields an id in a different shape (e.g. from a programmatic edge created elsewhere, or future React Flow versions), `target` is `undefined`, the `.map` matches no node, and the edge is silently orphaned with no error or log. Low impact today because the only edge creator is `onConnect`/`rfEdges` useMemo in this same file, but fragile if the edge id format ever changes. Guard with an explicit check: `if (!c.id.includes("->")) return;` and/or `console.warn` for diagnostics.

Three different `alert(...)` calls in this file (`doExport`, `doImport`, and the early return in `save`'s error path is via `handleCommandError`). Native `alert` blocks the renderer, looks out of place against the neumorphic UI styling, and is jarring mid-interaction. The codebase already has `handleCommandError` with structured error handling; consider adding a lightweight `notice(msg, kind: 'info' | 'success')` helper alongside it so success confirmations match the rest of the app's feedback style.

comments.content: `openWorkflow` does not reset `running` to `false` when switching workflows. If the user was viewing a running workflow (A) and opens a different non-running workflow (B), `running` stays `true` until the fire-and-forget `workflow_is_running` recheck resolves — and during that window the "停止" button is visible. Clicking it would call `workflow_stop` for workflow B (which isn't actually running) and the polling effect at line 474 only fires its first tick after 5s, so the wrong state can persist for seconds. Reset `running` to `false` synchronously at the top of `openWorkflow` (and `createBlank` already does this), letting the recheck flip it back to `true` only if B is genuinely running.

`useCallback` here returns a function that is immediately invoked on every render (`snapshot()` at line 134). The intent is to memoize the serialized snapshot, but `useCallback` only memoizes the function identity, not its result — `JSON.stringify` still runs on every render regardless of whether `name`/`goal`/`nodes` changed. Use `useMemo` to cache the serialized string and recompute only when deps change.

`stopRun` keeps `running` as `true` after the backend acknowledges stop and only updates it via the 300 ms recheck (`.catch(() => {})` silently swallows recheck failures). If the recheck invoke throws (e.g., backend unavailable) or returns `true` because the backend hasn't fully deregistered yet, the "停止" button stays visible indefinitely even though the workflow is no longer running. Set `running` to `false` optimistically after the successful `workflow_stop` ack so the UI flips immediately, then let the recheck flip it back to `true` only if backend disagrees.
